items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: The first band he built was Ben Pollack's band, in which Benny Goodman was at the time

ctx.x: What was Glenn Miller's, uh, what was Glenn Miller's, uh, aspiration at that time? Did he want to continue to be a jazz trombone player? Did he want to write even in those days?

He liked to, he liked to write more than anything. I'm going to tell you something that maybe you might not know. But Glenn Miller has built more bands, more jazz bands, than any man in the country. The first band he built was Ben Pollack's band, in which Benny Goodman was at the time, Jimmy Mac Paul and all those kind of guys. The next band he built was, uh, was Ray Noble's band when he came over here from England, which was the best band in the country at the time. Uh, he built the Claude Thornhill's, I think,…

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: I'm talking about when Benny Goodman and all those guys were with Pollock. And the band just couldn't cut his arrangement.

ctx.x: And you don't remember the ear of the word jazz?

No, no. If I said so, I'd be lying, Dick. I don't. This all of a sudden there it was. But even before, you know, I was a kid. But even before, I can go back this far, but even before they ever had jazz bands at all, ragtime bands or whatever you want to call them. You see, like I tell you, I had a card here of Fisher's Band where it was printed on it, Fisher's Ragtime Military Jazz Band. Now that's, when I first played, I was eight years old, that first job, the first parade I ever played. Now if I was born in…
This Fisher card. They used to call it Swing. This Fisher card, they'll call it Ragtime, not Jazz. Is that right? Huh? The Fisher, you mentioned Fisher.
